sections.content: How many people stayed in Gillingham after gaining qualifications?

Gillingham is a large town in the South East. Gillingham does not have its own university.

Gillingham has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Gillingham ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 5,305 state-school pupils from Gillingham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,640 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,600 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Gillingham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Gillingham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Gillingham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Gillingham move to?

Of Gillingham's graduates, 545 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 130 of those graduates (24%) were living fairly locally, in the Medway travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Gillingham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 450 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 260 of those qualified non-graduates (58%) were living fairly locally, in the Medway travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Gillingham's GCSE cohort:

  • 305 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 135 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 22% of graduates and 26% of qualified non-graduates living in Gillingham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,380 graduates and 1,530 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Gillingham. This is compared with the 1,640 graduates and 1,600 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of the graduates had also lived in Gillingham as GCSE pupils, while 22% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Gillingham in 2018 to 2019, 74% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 26% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
